title: Controllable User Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2605.11519v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Using offline datasets to evaluate conversational agents often fails to cover rare scenarios or to support testing new policies. This has motivated the use of controllable user simulators for targeted, counterfactual evaluation, typically implemented by prompting or fine-tuning large language models. In this work, we formalize controllable simulation as a causal inference problem. By bridging natural language evaluation with off-policy evaluation methodology, we show that the standard practice of training simulators via supervised fine-tuning on post-hoc trajectory labels yields a structurally biased model. Specifically, these labels are inextricably coupled to the data-generating behavior policy, injecting a look-ahead bias that breaks causal consistency. Furthermore, we prove that under policy shift this failure causes the variance of evaluation metrics to explode geometrically, a phenomenon we term controllability collapse.

translated_abstract: 使用离线数据集评估对话智能体往往无法覆盖罕见场景，也难以支持对新策略的测试。这促使人们采用可控用户模拟器来进行有针对性的、反事实的评估，其通常通过提示或微调大语言模型来实现。在本工作中，我们将可控模拟形式化为一个因果推断问题。通过将自然语言评估与离线策略评估方法相衔接，我们表明，通过在后验轨迹标签上进行监督微调来训练模拟器的标准做法会产生一个结构上有偏的模型。具体而言，这些标签与产生数据的行为策略不可避免地耦合在一起，注入了破坏因果一致性的前瞻偏差。此外，我们证明在策略偏移下，这种失败会导致评估指标的方差呈几何级数爆炸，我们将这一现象称为“可控性崩溃”。
tldr: 该论文将可控用户模拟形式化为因果推断问题，揭示了基于事后轨迹标签进行监督微调会引入破坏因果一致性的结构性前瞻偏差，并证明在策略偏移下这种失败会导致评估指标方差几何级数爆炸的“可控性崩溃”现象。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes controllable user simulation as a causal inference problem, revealing that supervised fine-tuning on post-hoc trajectory labels injects a structural look-ahead bias that breaks causal consistency, and proving that under policy shift this failure causes evaluation metric variance to explode geometrically—a phenomenon termed "controllability collapse."
